minutes.headline: Finance Committee reviewed the FY26 town/school budget and a citizen-petitioned $2M+ override; no votes were taken.
minutes.summary: The Finance Committee heard the town manager's final FY26 budget presentation department by department, including a $500,000 free-cash transfer to schools, restoration of the pavement management line by cutting a grant writer position, and a 14.84% town health insurance increase. It also received a citizen's petition for a Proposition 2½ override of over $2 million to restore school cuts, heard a detailed member critique of unreconciled school budget figures, and reviewed the full town meeting warrant; all votes and the annual report were deferred to next week.
not_audible: The exact dollar amount of the Marshall Park and municipal building design debt exclusions was not stated numerically.
The precise total override figure beyond 'over $2 million'/'two million and some change' was not stated as a single exact number.
The motorcycle lease's original annual cost was not stated.
Why police and fire fuel charge lines increased despite lower fuel prices was left unanswered pending follow-up.
The exact purpose of the Mass Bay Transportation cherry-sheet assessment was uncertain even to the finance director.
Several numeric figures rendered oddly by captions (e.g., '2,962 $263.4', '1,886 1522') could not be confirmed against a written document.
No vote counts were given for any warrant article discussion this meeting.

what_happened.line: Finance Committee heard the town manager's final FY26 budget department by department but took no votes, deferring decisions to next week.
A citizen's petition asks for a Proposition 2½ override to restore school budget cuts, with no committee position taken yet.
A committee member laid out discrepancies between school budget figures and staffing counts and will formally ask the school department to reconcile them before next week.
The town-side plan pairs a free-cash transfer to schools with cutting a grant-writer position to restore paving funds and absorbing a health insurance cost increase.
The committee will vote on every warrant article and finalize its town meeting report next week, holding a public hearing the same night.

why_it_matters: Town meeting voters will be asked to decide the override and every warrant article at the next session, which sets both the school and town tax impact for FY26.
The free-cash transfer and the health insurance increase affect whether this budget plan holds up without further cuts or a second ask next year.
The school budget's numbers were still being challenged as unreconciled, so figures voters see next week may shift before the vote.
watch_next: Finance Committee votes on all warrant articles and finalizes its annual report, with a public hearing the same night, next week's meeting.
Backup Zoom meeting Monday, April 7 at 7:00 pm if the report is not finished.

reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on the free cash, stabilization, special-projects and FY25 transfer figures and on most department totals once digit grouping is repaired. They differ on the attendee list, on several department totals (Facilities, Human Services, Culture and Recreation, Intergovernmental, Unclassified), and on decisions recorded by only one side. The official minutes are a summary and omit the sewer, OPEB and reserve-transfer discussion, while ours omit the override deferral and the annual-report option decision.
